title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
# Trapping Rain Water

Given `n` non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

## Example 1:

**Input:** height = [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]
**Output:** 6
**Explanation:** The above elevation map (black section) is represented by array [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1]. In this case, 6 units of rain water (blue section) are being trapped.

## Example 2:

**Input:** height = [4,2,0,3,2,5]
**Output:** 9

## Constraints:

*   `n == height.length`
*   `1 <= n <= 2 * 10^4`
*   `0 <= height[i] <= 10^5`

images.description: Trapping Rain Water visualization showing elevation map bar chart

solutions.name: Two Pointers - Optimal
solutions.description: Use two pointers and track max height from left and right. Water at each position = min(leftMax, rightMax) - height[i].

solutions.name: Dynamic Programming - Precompute Max
solutions.description: Precompute leftMax[i] and rightMax[i] arrays, then calculate water at each position.

solutions.name: Monotonic Stack
solutions.description: Use decreasing monotonic stack. When a taller bar is found, pop and calculate water bounded by popped bar.
